decision: Open event-messaging v1 as a peer V1 child of the dashboard platform roadmap, sequenced to lock after 2026-05-24-001-feat-dashboard-value-language-ia-v0 F001 lands and the IA copy map is canonical.
rationale: This plan converts raw technical notifications into layered messaging (headline + why + action + technical detail) across Discord, INBOX, terminal-notifier, and dashboard sinks. The translation table requires the IA copy map's value-first vocabulary as its source-of-truth; authoring it before IA F001 lands risks producing a second, divergent glossary. Inventory work is unblocked and complete (evidence/f001-inventory-draft.md); plan artifacts wait.

decision: F001 inventory complete; load-bearing findings: 27 INBOX event names vs 6 NotifyEvent kinds, ActionItem is a near-perfect superset of RenderedEvent, sanitization is render-ready, CLI parser construction is per-subcommand inline (no build_parser() factory exists), brand drift in body strings is widespread.
rationale: Inventory at docs/plans/2026-05-24-004-feat-event-messaging-v1/evidence/f001-inventory-draft.md is the load-bearing substrate input for plan drafting. The 27-vs-6 coverage gap expanded plan scope from 'improve copy' to 'improve copy + selectively expand notification surface'. The ActionItem superset finding informed the sidecar-merge pattern in D003.

decision: ActionItem bridge uses a sidecar-merge pattern: render produces ActionItems and writes them to a separate event-actions sidecar file under ~/.dontpanic/dashboard/, NOT directly into what-now.json. Dashboard build (operator_console / projects_dashboard) merges the sidecar into what-now.json at build time alongside provider-derived ActionItems.
rationale: Direct push into what-now.json from dispatch_event would risk clobbering provider-derived dashboard cache and make advisory notification flow mutate the primary dashboard artifact. The sidecar pattern preserves the read-only-by-default invariant: notification flow writes to its own file; the dashboard build retains ownership of what-now.json. Pull-from-INBOX (machine-A-emit, machine-B-dashboard-reads) stays V4 team/realtime work.

decision: F002 NotifyEvent metadata extension is in scope. Add fields: subtype, breaker_kind, iteration_count, feature_display_name, aggregate_class, blocking, target_env, target_project. Add NotifyEvent dispatch at six high-value silent emit sites: verdict_mismatch, no_progress_classification, environmental_blocker_short_circuit, verdict_blocked_reconciled, gate_state_reconciliation_failed, architecture_regen_failed.
rationale: Earlier scope claim 'only renderer changes, no emit-point changes' was wrong per architect/PM critique. NotifyEvent today carries free-form markdown body + minimal headers; structured rendering keyed off discriminators requires those fields. The six new emit sites surface high-severity events that are currently INBOX-only or terminal-only. INBOX writes precede dispatch in every case (existing invariant preserved).

decision: action_link aliases evidence_uri rather than being renamed. Both fields accept the same value; new code populates evidence_uri; old code paths that read action_link continue working. Deprecate action_link after sinks and tests migrate.
rationale: Semantic overlap is total per inventory Section 6. Hard rename in a single pass would touch every emit site, every sink, every test. Alias-then-deprecate is the safe migration pattern. Also aligns the NotifyEvent field name with the ActionItem field name already used by the dashboard.

decision: feature_display_name is computed at the emit site where loaded.feature(feature_id) is already in scope. event_copy module provides a fallback (use feature_id when display name is missing) but never reaches back into plan loading.
rationale: Every supervisor emit site already has loaded in scope. Computing the display name once at emit (loaded.feature(feature_id).get('description', '')) keeps event_copy a pure renderer with no I/O dependency on the plan loader. Fallback to feature_id in event_copy preserves rendering when emit sites don't populate the field.

decision: Every INBOX event kind receives an explicit translation disposition: live, dashboard_action, inbox_only, or audit_only. Only selected high-value kinds render to Discord/terminal and/or produce dashboard ActionItems. Disposition is part of the translation table, not an implicit rendering side effect.
rationale: Earlier framing 'all 27 INBOX kinds render across 4 sinks' was too broad. Many events (architecture_regenerated, pre_impl_status_synced, gate_cleared, resumed, defer_cleared) are durable-audit-only and would create notification noise if surfaced live. The disposition layer is the v1 decision surface: which events deserve operator attention, which are audit-trail-only. Disposition is data, reviewed and revised independent of rendering logic.

decision: Where no canonical CLI remediation exists, render explanation + evidence_uri with exact_command=None. No invented commands. Applies to: gate_state_reconciliation_failed (no auto-reconcile subcommand exists), verdict_mismatch (no plan-reaudit subcommand), generic error (site-dependent context).
rationale: Per architect/PM critique earlier in this thread: 'wrong commands in fixtures are worse than the current technical copy because operators copy-and-paste failures.' If event_copy cannot produce a verifiable canonical command, the field is None and the rendering surfaces the explanation only. F001 command-validation harness enforces this: every populated exact_command must parse against the real CLI; otherwise the renderer must produce None.

decision: breaker:patch_incomplete keeps its colon-separated event name in INBOX for backward compatibility with existing INBOX parsers. New structured rendering normalizes internally to event=breaker_tripped with breaker_kind=patch_incomplete; existing parsers continue to see the legacy event name.
rationale: Inventory Section 2 notes patch_completeness_gate.py:261-269 emits with the colon separator (the only event using : in its name). Hard rename would break any external INBOX parser that pattern-matches event names. Internal normalization gives the new event_copy module the structured field it needs (breaker_kind) without breaking compatibility. Migration to clean naming can happen in a later cleanup with explicit forward-compat planning.

decision: Brand drift fix is in scope. event_copy translates all jarvis approve / jarvis-orchestrate approve / Jarvis [plan_id] references in rendered output to dontpanic equivalents. Source body strings in supervisor.py and elsewhere are NOT edited as part of this plan; translation happens at the render boundary.
rationale: Inventory Section 2 'Brand drift' confirms body strings reference legacy jarvis commands at supervisor.py:335, 801-804, 990-1004, and in multiple notify.notify titles. Editing every source string is a separate cleanup. Translating at the render boundary contains the scope and ensures every channel emits correct dontpanic commands regardless of source body content. Source-side cleanup can be a separate small PR.

decision: Sanitization at render boundary uses existing operator_console._assert_no_secret_shapes + _walk_strings (raise mode) for the dashboard sidecar write path, and state_projection._redact (substitute mode) for live Discord/terminal/INBOX paths. No regex changes required; no new sanitization module.
rationale: Inventory Section 5 confirms the 9-pattern regex tuple at sanitization_check.py:92-102 is already loaded by three surfaces and is generic over dict[str, Any]. Raise mode is correct for the sidecar (operator-fixable failure before write) but wrong for live notifications (Discord/terminal shouldn't fail-hard the supervisor). Two modes already exist; F004 picks per surface. The brief's reference to a '45-case sanitization matrix' was wrong — that number was the Discord plan's test matrix (3 levels x 3 webhook states x 5 event kinds). Real sanitization is 9 regex patterns.

decision: Side-effect-free command validation uses a token-only validator (Approach 2) for v1, not full per-subcommand parser-factory extraction (Approach 1). A new scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/command_validation.py module enumerates subcommand vocabulary and expected token shapes. Parser-factory extraction is recorded as a deferred-quality move and not blocked by this plan.
rationale: Inventory Section 4 confirms parser construction is per-subcommand inline across ~18 subcommand functions (~10 LoC each). Approach 1 unlocks downstream value (shell completion, doc generation) but is a substantial mechanical refactor. Approach 2 ships in days, validates command shape against a declared vocabulary, and is sufficient for event_copy's needs ('is this command well-formed enough to render in copy'). Drift risk (new flags not in validator) is mitigated by a round-trip test asserting every subcommand accepts every validator-approved shape. Future plan may upgrade to Approach 1.

decision: INBOX append_event() signature is unchanged; truth-of-record invariant preserved. event_copy.render() produces a RenderedEvent; sinks consume RenderedEvent. INBOX adds an additive wrapper append_rendered_event() that calls append_event(raw) first, then appends the rendered markdown block (with <details> for technical metadata) so INBOX retains both raw audit entry and human-readable rendering.
rationale: Per architect/PM correction earlier: 'INBOX remains truth-of-record; richer rendering is an output mode, not a replacement for raw event recording.' Audit reconstruction continues from raw entries unchanged; operators reading INBOX get the readable rendering inline; old emit sites that call only append_event() continue working without modification.

decision: Capability live notifications (capability_blocked, capability_ready_after_setup, etc.) are deferred. Dashboard capability ActionItems continue to be provider-derived from StatusEnvelope. No NotifyEvent emit sites added in capability subsystem during this plan.
rationale: Inventory Section 6 + Q10 notes the capability subsystem emits no NotifyEvent today; dashboard providers consume StatusEnvelope directly. Adding live capability events expands plan scope into a new emit-point subsystem with its own state machine and is not necessary for the messaging-quality fix. Logged for a possible V2+ follow-on plan if cross-machine capability awareness becomes a real need.

decision: volley_start double-write at supervisor.py:1477 + supervisor.py:1532-1540 is filed as a separate bug, not bundled into this plan. Bug fix is independent of messaging quality work and should ship as a small focused commit.
rationale: Inventory Section 6 'Coverage gap: double-write at volley_start' confirms the duplicate INBOX entry within a single dispatch. Bundling unrelated bug fixes into this plan would muddy its scope and audit trail. Track separately and reference from this plan's evidence if useful, but do not let it block messaging-quality lock.

decision: Plan artifacts (plan.md, features.json, objective_contract.json) are NOT drafted until 2026-05-24-001-feat-dashboard-value-language-ia-v0 F001 lands and the IA copy map is canonical. This decisions.jsonl is written first to lock architectural commitments while IA work proceeds in parallel.
rationale: Per architect/PM agreement: 'I'd proceed with a hold until IA F001 is canonical, but the planning decisions above are enough to draft decisions.jsonl now without committing copy.' Capturing decisions early preserves the architectural commitments durably; copy authoring waits for canonical IA vocabulary so the messaging translation table can reference IA copy map keys rather than authoring a parallel glossary.

decision: NotifyEvent gains an inbox_event field (the INBOX event= value at the paired append_event call) plus a technical_metadata dict[str, str|int|bool|None] for kind-specific long-tail data. The translation table in event_copy is keyed by inbox_event, NOT by NotifyEvent.kind. The 8 first-class fields named in D004 keep their first-class status; technical_metadata catches everything else (verdict_mismatch's narrative_verdict/structured_status/audit_path, defer_tripped's defer_gate/dispatch_class, volley_terminal's final_status/rounds, gate_state_reconciliation_failed's persisted_state_path, etc.).
rationale: Architect/PM review finding #1+#2: F003 translation table claimed to key by 'real INBOX event_name' but NotifyEvent only carries kind today, and the vocabularies differ (gate_paused vs gate_hit, signoff vs INBOX volley_terminal). Without an inbox_event field on NotifyEvent, the renderer can't look up the disposition table. F002 also referenced fields (narrative_verdict, structured_status, audit_path) it did not define. Solution: add inbox_event as the translation key + technical_metadata as the long-tail bag. Keeps NotifyEvent dataclass extension small (10 new fields total: 1 key + 8 first-class + 1 dict) while accommodating all kind-specific data.

decision: INBOX additive wrapper appends ONLY the rendered markdown block. Existing emit sites continue to call append_event() directly for the raw truth-of-record entry; the dispatch flow additionally calls append_rendered_annotation() after dispatch_event for live and dashboard_action dispositions. The wrapper does NOT call append_event() internally. Renamed from append_rendered_event() to append_rendered_annotation() to make the additive-block-only semantic explicit.
rationale: Architect/PM review finding #3: The proposed append_rendered_event() wrapper called append_event() internally, but existing emit sites already call append_event() before dispatch. Result would have been duplicate raw entries in INBOX. Fix: wrapper appends ONLY the rendered annotation block; raw append at emit sites is unchanged. Rename to append_rendered_annotation() to remove ambiguity about whether the function writes the raw event too.

decision: Sidecar merge happens at BOTH write paths: (a) dashboard.build() before render_json writes out_dir/what-now.json, AND (b) operator_console.write_cache() before writing the dashboard home cache. A shared helper merge_with_event_sidecar(provider_items) -> list[ActionItem] is called from both sites.
rationale: Architect/PM review finding #4: dashboard.build() writes out_dir/what-now.json via render_json(items) BEFORE operator_console.write_cache() is called (see scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/dashboard.py:310). Extending only write_cache() would leave the served dashboard state stale because the build-time write doesn't see the sidecar. Both write paths must merge or the operator opens a dashboard that's missing event-derived ActionItems.

decision: Promote state_projection._scrub_secrets to a public scrub_secrets symbol for the live-notification redact path. Keep the private name as a backward-compat alias if existing imports reference it.
rationale: Architect/PM review finding #5: F004 originally referenced state_projection._redact, but the actual existing helper is state_projection._scrub_secrets (private). Binding new code to a private symbol couples implementation detail. Promoting to public is a one-line cosmetic change that lets the new event_copy / sink renderers reference state_projection.scrub_secrets cleanly.

decision: command_validation test suite is purely token-based. It does NOT call _<cmd>_main(argv) or any subcommand handler. Vocabulary drift mitigation is manual PR discipline: when a new subcommand or flag lands in cli.py, the validator vocabulary update lands in the same PR.
rationale: Architect/PM review finding #6: F001 originally proposed a 'round-trip vocabulary test' that confirmed every validator-declared subcommand was accepted by its corresponding _<cmd>_main(argv). But those _<cmd>_main functions parse AND execute together; calling them would trigger real side effects (plan loader mutations, gate state writes, subprocess dispatches, network calls). Per D012 the validator is token-only specifically to avoid these side effects. The round-trip test would have violated the same invariant the validator exists to enforce. Drop the round-trip test; rely on manual PR review when adding new subcommands/flags.

decision: Discord embed colors use inline hex literals from the IA copy map band tokens (healthy=0x3DD68C, action=0xF5A623, blocked=0xF25555, pending=0x7E8BA6). NO dependency on a dp-tokens.css file (no such asset exists in this repo as of plan draft time).
rationale: Architect/PM review finding #7: F003 originally referenced dp-tokens.css for embed colors. The Claude Design manifest names that file but it has not been committed to the repo (no file exists under docs/design/ or dashboard/). Embed colors are simple hex values — inline them from the copy map's documented 4-band taxonomy rather than introducing a runtime CSS dependency that doesn't exist. If a tokens file is committed later, this is a trivial follow-up replacement.
